question: India's rank in the Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI) decline from _____ in 2022 to _____ in 2023.
solution:
The correct answer is __**85; 93**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India's rank in the **Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI)** declined from **85th** in 2022 to **93rd** in 2023.
 
• The CPI, published annually by **Transparency International**, assesses perceived levels of public sector corruption across 180 countries and territories, with scores ranging from 0 (highly corrupt) to 100 (very clean).
 
• A **lower score and rank indicate higher perceived corruption**.
 
• This decline suggests a growing perception of corruption in India's public sector, highlighting the need for enhanced anti-corruption measures and governance reforms to improve transparency and accountability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Top Performers (2023):** Denmark, Finland, and New Zealand retained their positions as the least corrupt nations, with scores exceeding 88.
 
• **Bottom Performers (2023):** Countries like Somalia, South Sudan, and Syria ranked the lowest, with scores below 15.
 
• To improve its standing in the CPI, India must:
 
• Strengthen institutions like the **Central Vigilance Commission (CVC)**.
 
• Promote public awareness and transparency in governance.
 
• Foster collaborations with international organizations to implement best practices for combating corruption.
